performance.status: source prepared; no measured result or performance acceptance

inputPins.newMixedCorpus: The native reference must be committed in the clean candidate before launch. Its exact git blob, SHA-256, capture/source/toolchain identities and all artifact hashes are frozen before the first child; workers reject changes. No uncaptured artifact hash is invented.

guardProtocol: Both preparation children generate identical structural bytes, decode the same pinned real image and compare complete reader fields, field order, scalar rows, all heap bytes, referenced heap values, list/type callbacks and owned/borrowed contracts before any timing.

Default readPE method-body outcomes and section RVA conversions are compared outside timing. Inspection-only reads additionally check all five retained native method CIL byte sequences; expected default unsupported outcomes remain explicit.

Every timed reader result is consumed and compared outside timing, including all returned data fields, field order, borrowed stream buffers and PE input identity. Full callback/ownership facts are rechecked after timing.

All four candidate-only bounded controls use maxRows equal to the actual physical row total; readPE forwards that value in metadataOptions. One less must reject with MD_READ_ROW_LIMIT before timing. Signal is omitted in both default and bounded controls.

The candidate-only feature child first replays every retained mixed native fact. Construction and append returns are guarded by complete history snapshots; all mapping, latest/historical row and four-heap query returns are checked against the replay-qualified expectations.

No feature module is imported by baseline reader children or the parent. Two fixed worker dynamic imports are bound to a single exact source hash/count allowlist entry and checked before loading public aliases.

measurement.statistics: True median; nearest-rank p95 and p99 of the 100 chronological batch means, never individual-call latency percentiles
measurement.counts: Four default controls on each side, four separately labeled candidate row-budget controls, eight new-feature workloads: 20 workloads and 2400 total warm/measured batches.
measurement.timed: Synchronous public invocation plus one assignment of its returned value into a preallocated array
measurement.outsideTiming: Imports/startup, input preparation, native replay, prerequisite history construction, correctness guards, disposal, output serialization, statistics and I/O
measurement.memory: Signed net heapUsed deltas and process memory observations; GC can make deltas negative and ArrayBuffer/native allocation is not fully represented. No total allocation counter or peak-RSS claim.
measurement.features: Construction uses the mixed baseline PE. Appends use fresh preceding histories prepared outside timing. Four named entity probes and four heap probes use fixed equal round-robin mixes. Latest/historical rows target Added at generations 2/1.

retention: Retain the entire new benchmark destination: report.json, inputs.json, all fifteen job/result records, and every stdout/stderr log, including failed attempts and partial worker records.
The report records exact Node argv/cwd, job/source/tool/native/fixture hashes, own package entries, process statuses/times, node/V8/CPU/OS/environment and raw chronological warm/measured samples.
Retain the outer limited-wrapper command, raw log, environment, status/signal and artifact SHA-256 inventory separately under qualification.
Copy evidence byte-for-byte into qualification/performance-first only after capture finishes; do not write evidence into either measured checkout during the run.

Independently recompute all statistics from raw samples. Preserve original figures, absolute costs and every regression. More than 5% existing median regression needs quantified justification and explicit PR sign-off; the driver never grants acceptance.
An interrupted process may not have written its current in-memory samples. Preserve its raw exit/log/result absence honestly; never fill missing observations or silently replace the cohort.
